intent: Authoritative in the field; frequently knows more about the specifics than the piece will cover.
domain_familiarity: Authoritative: publishes, reviews, or sets standard practice in the field.
purpose: Wants the specific new claim, evidence, or method detail — nothing that re-derives what they already know.
assumed_knowledge: the full domain vocabulary and its method literature
edge cases and known failure modes of standard approaches

text.explanation_depth: state the claim and its evidence directly; no scaffolding explanation of established concepts
text.section_granularity: may be a single dense section; no obligation to segment for pacing

visual.label_density: higher label density is acceptable than for any other audience
visual.legend: legend may be omitted for domain-standard encodings

audio.thought_unit_length: long, unbroken technical passages are acceptable
audio.term_glossing: no glossing; jargon-dense delivery is expected and preferred

anti_patterns: Explaining what the expert already knows
Hedging an established fact to make the piece read as more accessible
Padding to reach an expected length instead of stopping when the new claim is made
Adding a legend or acronym expansion the expert audience does not need, diluting information density
